name: parkland
note: The Classic Parkland pack on Meshy, the first landscape of the US golf courses work (the owner, 5 November 2026). Trees are taller and narrower than the game's rounded hand-built ones, as trees on real courses are, and stand in the open with grass to the trunk. Heights, widths and trunk widths are PLACED from the species' usual forest-grown form and the owner's course photos, so look at them against the pictures. Colours start from the game's own (oak #487039, maple #658d36, spruce #2c5349); the elm and tulip poplar colours are placed. Both pin oaks were sent back by the owner as pine-shaped and rewritten as oval and untiered. Shipped in vendor/blender-meshy_parkland, with AmericanElm as ParkElm and TulipPoplar as ParkPoplar because the hand-built models hold those names. `seasons` are each species' colours, PLACED, read by tools/blender/dump-tints.mjs. American elm has one version: elm 2 came out nearly bare and the owner dropped it. Targets match the Redwood Coast's biggest trees, the young redwoods at 12,600 (the owner, 6 November 2026): 12,000 triangles for a broadleaf, 12,600 for the spruce. They were about 6,000 and 7,300 until the owner asked why these trees should have less detail than the redwoods. The cost on Low is still to be measured.
style: Stylised cartoon game art in soft, flat painted colour. Simple clean shapes with a gentle gradient: darker near the trunk and under each bough, lighter toward the tips. Matte, muted natural palette. No photographic detail, no photo bark, no noise, no speckle, no hard shadows, no highlights, no shine, no ink outlines, no text.
view: One view only, seen from the side at eye level, the whole plant in frame from foot to tip with a margin around it, centred, on a plain white background, in even soft light, with no cast shadow.

models.name: Blender_WhiteOak_1

models.prompt: A mature white oak tree on a parkland golf course, 28 m tall and 16 m wide, clearly taller than it is wide. Straight pale grey trunk with shallow scaly bark, running high up into the crown before it divides, bare for its lowest quarter. Eight to twelve strong tapering limbs angle upward and outward. Each limb ends in one large solid rounded tuft of foliage, like a soft fluffy cloud, with a lightly tufted scalloped edge, and smaller tufts sit between them. The tufts are chunky, overlap only a little, and together make a tall irregular oval crown with a bumpy uneven outline. Sky and limbs show through the gaps between the tufts. Paint the foliage as thick, solid three-dimensional forms, never as separate leaves: no visible leaves, no leaf shapes, no lobes, no fine detail, no thin lines, no thin wisps, nothing thinner than a limb. No solid core, no perfect spheres, no round lollipop shape, no even tiers of branches, no Christmas tree outline, no acorns. A slender trunk, one twentieth of the tree's height wide near the ground, narrowing gently to two-thirds of that width at mid-height and to thick limbs at the top, its sides never parallel. Only a small flare in the very bottom of the trunk, no wide base. Whole healthy tree, no broken or snapped top. Stylised cartoon game asset, matte hand-painted colour.
